title: Session affinity tracing and tenant cost dashboard guide
content:
Purpose
This note lays out a pragmatic approach for instrumenting session-affinity traces across the inference stack and using the enriched traces to drive tenant-aware cost dashboards. Goal is to give platform owners and dashboard authors a clear, actionable recipe (metrics, span conventions, sampling rules, dashboard widgets, and ownership) so that we can: 1) attribute cost to tenants and routes with reasonable accuracy, 2) investigate tail latency and per-session degradation, and 3) keep dashboard query cost manageable.

Context and motivation
- Problem: With multi-tenant Dedicated and Hosted traffic, cost and latency issues often surface at the tenant level, but our current telemetry is scoped to service-level aggregates. This makes it hard to: spot tenants that generate disproportionate token cost, debug session-specific latency regressions caused by kv-cache misses, or correlate model fallback frequency with tenant config.
- Opportunity: Use session IDs + lightweight tracing context to connect token counts, kernel time, and cache behavior per logical session without exploding cardinality.

High-level design
1) Session affinity propagation
   - Every incoming request (hosted/dedicated) must carry a single session_id (UUIDv4-ish). For ad-hoc short stateless requests, generate a transient session id labeled "stateless" so dashboards can optionally filter.
   - Propagate session_id through HTTP headers and internal RPCs: X-RW-Session, X-RW-Tenant, X-RW-Route, X-RW-Sequence (optional).

2) Trace/span naming and attributes (convention)
   - Root span: serve.request
       attrs: session_id, tenant_id, route, model, seq_len, client_region
   - Child spans:
       - parsing (serve.request.parse) -> attrs: prompt_tokens, system_tokens
       - routing (serve.request.route) -> attrs: model_variant, fallback_reason (if any)
       - kernel.exec (serve.kernel.exec) -> attrs: gpu_ms, cpu_ms, peak_mem_mb, quantized (y/n)
       - kv_cache.lookup (serve.kvcache.lookup) -> attrs: kv_hit (bool), prefix_len, cached_tokens
       - network.outbound (serve.net.out) -> attrs: bytes_sent, stream (bool)
   - Prefer short dot-separated names. Keep span attr keys stable across services.

3) Sampling strategy (cost-aware, session-centric)
   - Default low-rate trace sampling (0.5%-1%) for full traces across all traffic to control storage cost.
   - Forced sampling (100%) for error or anomaly signals: any 5xx, model fallback, large token spikes (>10k tokens), explicit SRE trace flags.
   - Adaptive session sampling: if a session exhibits >X% kv_cache_miss over Y requests or token rate above threshold, escalate sampling for subsequent requests in that session for N minutes.

4) Metrics to emit (names & semantics)
   - telemetry.request.count (counter): incremented per request, labels: tenant_id, route, model, outcome(success|error|fallback)
   - telemetry.request.tokens_produced (counter): tokens generated in response, labels: tenant_id, model_variant
   - telemetry.kernel.ms (histogram): per kernel.exec span duration, labels: model_variant, gpu_type, quantized
   - telemetry.kvcache.hit_ratio (gauge or derived): prefer derived from hits / lookups over a rolling window per tenant/route
   - telemetry.tenant.estimated_cost_per_1k_tokens (gauge): derived cost estimate using model profile + infra rate
   - telemetry.streams.active (gauge): active streaming connections by region/route
   - telemetry.trace.sample_rate_effective (gauge): runtime sampled fraction (for debugging sampling coverage)

5) Low-cardinality aggregation policy
   - Primary dashboards must aggregate at tenant_id and route, but avoid adding model_variant or gpu_type as high-cardinality filters by default. Expose them as drilldowns only.
   - For kv-cache metrics, emit both a global per-service bucket and a per-tenant sample set (sampled sessions) to approximate miss rates without per-tenant high-cardinality metrics for every minute.

Dashboard composition (recommended widgets)
- Tenant cost heatmap: rows=tenant_id (top 50 by spend), cols=7-day cost trend. Source: telemetry.request.tokens_produced * cost_profile(model).
- Session tail latency table: top 50 slow sessions (p95 p99), link to trace id and span breakdown (kernel vs net vs parsing).
- KV-cache telemetry: bucketed hit_ratio distribution; small panel showing sampled session traces where kv_cache.lookup.kv_hit=false and kernel time spikes.
- Fallback scatter: x=token_count, y=fallback_rate by tenant, size=average_latency. Useful to detect large inputs causing fallbacks.
- Sampling coverage widget: show effective sampling % and number of forced traces to ensure observability quality.
- Drilldown panel: tenant -> recent traces list (last 24h) with quick link to open trace in tracing UI.

Instrumentation checklist (developer-facing)
- Add session_id propagation header at edge (ingress): X-RW-Session. Backfill flag: if missing, generate and mark "session_source=generated".
- Ensure every service attaches session_id to trace root and adds tenant_id label to metrics.
- Annotate kernel.exec spans with gpu_ms and quantized tags. Do not emit per-request raw token lists in spans.
- Emit telemetry.request.tokens_produced as a counter; derive token_rate in aggregator.
- Implement adaptive sampling hook in edge router (link to PR in linked_artifacts).

Ownership and runbook snippets
- Dashboard owner: Observability / Cost Analytics (primary: Priya Nair, backup: Julian Ortiz).
- Tracing schema steward: eng-serving-runtime (Samir Gupta).
- SRE alert rules: create alerts when top-5 tenant cost drift >20% week-over-week or when kv_cache.median_miss_rate > 15% for any high-spend tenant.
- Debug flow: 1) From dashboard find tenant -> open session tail latency -> open trace -> inspect kernel.exec vs kvcache.lookup -> check recent rollout changes (link to GH/Release notes).

Query cost and retention considerations
- Keep 7-day retention for granular per-tenant cost windows, 30-day retention for aggregated rollups.
- Avoid running heavy per-tenant time series in dashboards by computing daily rollups offline and surfacing them as lightweight series.

Migration/rollout plan (6 weeks)
- Week 0: proto instrument on staging with session_id and minimal spans; validate in synthetic tests.
- Week 1-2: enable adaptive sampling on 5% of production requests; collect sampling coverage metrics.
- Week 3-4: onboard cost-estimate pipeline (offline job) and create tenant heatmap dashboard in read-only mode.
- Week 5: open beta to internal product & cs teams for feedback.
- Week 6: enable public dashboards and configure alerts.

Open questions and tradeoffs
- Cardinality vs fidelity: how many tenant labels do we keep on raw metrics? Proposal: keep tenant_id only on a small set of counters and rely on sampled traces for deep dives.
- Cost model accuracy: we use model profiles + quantization multipliers — need validation against actual infra billing.
- Privacy: for regulated tenants, provide opt-out (do not store session traces; only emit aggregated metrics).

Todo / next steps
- [ ] Finalize header names and add to telemetry coding standard (Samir).
- [ ] Land adaptive sampling PR and validate on staging (link in linked_artifacts).
- [ ] Create dashboard mockups and get sign-off from Cost Analytics (Priya).
- [ ] Run a 2-week smoke test and compare estimated costs to infra billing (owner: Julian).

Notes / references
- Slack channel: #observability (use thread OBS-session-affinity)
- Linear: OBS-412 (session affinity sampling)
- GH PR: telemetry/pull/124 (adaptive sampling hook)

Quick copy-paste for instrumenters
- Header assignment at ingress: set X-RW-Session: <uuid4> and X-RW-Tenant: <tenant_id>
- Trace root attrs: {"session_id": "...", "tenant_id": "...", "route": "...", "model": "..."}

Appendix: example metric queries (pseudocode)
- tenant_tokens_7d(tenant_id) = sum(telemetry.request.tokens_produced{tenant_id=tenant_id}[7d])
- tenant_est_cost(tenant_id) = tenant_tokens_7d(tenant_id) * model_cost_lookup(model_variant) / 1000
- sample_kv_miss_sessions = topk(50, rate(telemetry.kvcache.lookup_total{kv_hit="false"}[10m]))

End of note.

Comments welcome — especially on the sampling knobs and the budget impact of increased forced traces.
